summary: B is the less invasive patch, but neither candidate satisfies the frozen contract and neither should merge unchanged.
reasons: Both expose Upload with opts ...UploadFileOption instead of the required opts ...FilesOption.
Both bypass FilesService.Add and duplicate its Raw.Do request, response-decoding, and missing-data logic.
Both add forbidden association-option APIs and modify generic retry machinery beyond the requested scope.

B preserves the existing WithFilesQuery and WithFilesRequestOptions signatures; A changes their return types and adds overlapping option interfaces, creating avoidable API-compatibility and maintenance risk even though the returned values still implement FilesOption normally used at call sites that invoke them directly rather than storing the function itself e.g. var f func(url.Values) FilesOption = WithFilesQuery would break due to exact function signature mismatch in Go; any reflection/docs generated API also changes. This is concrete source compatibility risk despite gates passing because compatibility suite may not test function value assignment. Also A's FilesRequestOption embedding UploadFileOption means future custom FilesOption implementations can't be used Upload, violating contract anyway. B leaves old API untouched while wrong new API. That's meaningful preference. But note B's public WithUpload* extras also violate exact add convenience only. Both broaden helper for fields rather than direct NewFile, contrary reuse. B uses NewForm wrapping NewFile; A NewFileWithFields. Both technically preserve NewFile's behavior but duplicate machinery extension. The raw seek retry changes themselves address first report but frozen says not to refactor. B test with nonseekable io.MultiReader proves Upload's buffered multipart body can be retried regardless source replayability, matching streamed-content requirement more directly than A's os.File upload test. A separately tests Add raw os.File but out-of-scope. Neither includes source-reader error test. A's validation combines errors vs B distinct, but both validate before request. A's generic raw helper computes content length by seeking to end and assumes failed Seek leaves offset untouched, which io.Seeker doesn't guarantee—potential data corruption. B only seeks current and later start, simpler. Both GetBody closure uses same seeker, okay sequential retries but unsafe concurrent cloning; requests aren't concurrently retried. B doesn't set ContentLength, chunked, acceptable. Both changing closer semantics out-of-scope. B docs says io.ReadSeeker retry on 429/502... perhaps true. A extra docs huge. B more reviewable.
risks_a: Changes existing option-constructor return types, which can break assignments expecting the exact function type even though ordinary calls still work.
Adds multiple public option interfaces, association helpers, arbitrary form fields, and multipart-helper machinery explicitly excluded by the contract.
Its seek-to-end retry helper assumes a failed Seek leaves the reader offset intact, which io.Seeker does not guarantee.
risks_b: Upload has the wrong option type and therefore cannot accept established FilesOption implementations as required.
Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of Add, duplicating behavior and risking future semantic drift.
Adds forbidden association APIs and broad Raw.Do replay/closing behavior changes, and lacks a source-reader failure test.
